Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

represent verb

act or speak for

also on behalf of, in the name of, speak for, stand in for

classical

Cic. Off. 1.124: intellegere sē gerere persōnam cīvitātis
M-O s.v. represent: persōnam gerere

persōnam gerere

phrase: persōnam with the genitive of whom one represents

represent, act for (a person, a body)

Persōna is the actor’s mask and so the part one plays; persōnam sustinēre is the same (Cic. Pis. 24, Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens also give vicem gerere.

Other words

  • nōmine — on behalf of, in the name of

    the ablative of nōmen, with a genitive or a possessive: meō, tuō nōmine · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.16.16: tuō nōmine grātiās ēgī; Cic. Att. 3.15.8: meō nōmine litterās darī

  • repraesentō, repraesentāre, repraesentāvī, repraesentātum — not “act for”: classically, bring before the mind, show; portray; pay at once

    verb, first conjugation · avoid · classical · Quint. 6.2.29; Plin. NH 34.88 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short give “bring before one, show, exhibit”, “represent, portray” (of artists, post-Augustan) and, in trade, “pay on the spot”; never acting on someone’s behalf.

Examples

  • Est igitur proprium mūnus magistrātūs intellegere sē gerere persōnam cīvitātis

    It is, then, the particular duty of a magistrate to understand that he represents the stateCic. Off. 1.124

  • Antōniō tuō nōmine grātiās ēgī

    I thanked Antonius on your behalfCic. Att. 1.16.16

  • sī quī erunt quibus putēs opus esse meō nōmine litterās darī, velim cōnscrībās cūrēsque dandās

    if there is anyone you think should have a letter in my name, please write it and see that it is deliveredCic. Att. 3.15.8

See also role, mean, represent.

SourcesLewis & Short: persona · Lewis & Short: gero · Lewis & Short: nomen · Lewis & Short: repraesento

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. represent.
